To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the increased capacity for zeanthin-independent dissipa-tion of energy exceeding the photosynthetic capacity in Pinus bank-siana under simulated autumn conditions was due to a reduced rate in electron transport from the cyt b6f complex and not a reduced electron transport from PSII to PSI.
the capacity for zeaxantin-independent dissipation in P. banksia exceeds its photochemical capacity when exposed to increased autumn air temperatures.

an increase in autumnal air temperature inhibits photosynthesis in P. banksia by decreasing the efficiency in energy transfer between the antenna and the photosystem II reaction center and by decreasing electron transport from the thylakoid electron transport chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological and biochemical responses of plants to the environmental conditions in autumn.
the physiological responses of boreal trees to the changing climate.
the effects of climate change on photosynthetic processes in boreal trees, with the aim of predicting future productivity and growth of boreal forests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increased air temperature of SD/HT treatment results in a decreased photosynthetic electron transfer rate from photosystem II to photosystem I, which in turn results in an inhibition of electron transfer from the cyto-chrome b6f complex.

the photosynthetic capacity of boreal conifers is impaired under increased air temperature during the autumn period, with a reduced capacity for electron transport from photosystem II to photosystem I as the major factor.

the increased air temperature in autumn inhibits the photosynthetic capacity of P. banksiana through the inhibition of electron transport from photosystem II to photosystem I, which results in a decreased capacity for CO2 assimilation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the capacity of the plant to dissipate energy in excess of the photochemical capacity is not impaired by increased temperature in autumn conditions, but rather the capacity for photosynthesis is limited by the capacity of intersystem electron transport.
the capacity for photosynthesis in P. banksia is limited during autumn by a reduced photosynthetic electron flow between photosystem II and photosystem I.
the photosynthetic apparatus in plants exposed to increased autumn air temperatures is less able to utilize the available energy, resulting in a decreased capacity to produce biomass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a decrease in the ratio of PSII to PSI in the SD/HT treatment is associated with a decrease in the rate of electron flow through the cytochrome complex and a decrease in the amount of Rubisco.

the effect of climate warming in autumn on the photosynthetic performance of boreal trees is not simply a matter of temperature but rather the interaction of photoperiod, temperature and photoprotection.
the effects of climate change on plant physiology are complex and depend on the interaction between multiple factors.
